To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Repaglinide and rosiglitazone have similar effects on glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The new insulin secretagogue, repaglinides (Novo Nordisk), has been shown to be more effective than glibenclamide (Aventis Pharma) in reducing HbA1c levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
1. In patients with diabetes, the new insulin secretogues, repag-linide and nategli-nide, are effective and safe in lowering HbA1C and are well tolerated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure, dynamics and function of the proteins involved in the process of insulin release.
the synthesis and characterization of new materials for the treatment of diabetes.
the development and application of novel materials for use in the treatment of diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the newer insulin secretagogues do have advantages over the sulfonylures, but they do so at a cost that will have to be justified by their ability to improve outcomes in patients with diabetes.
repaglinide, like nateglinide and the older sulfonylurease, has its niche and is useful in the appropriate clinical situation.
the new insulin secretagogue class of drugs is a welcome addition to our armamentarium for the treatment of type 2 diabetic patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in a new era of diabetes treatment.
the new insulin secretagous have a more rapid onset of insulin secretion, a shorter duration of action, a greater effect in the early hours after meals, and a greater risk of hypoglycemic reactions.
the newer agents are not superior to glyburide in terms of glycemic control or side-effect profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the new insulin secretagouges, nateglinide and repaglinide, are effective and safe in the treatment of type 2 diabetic patients.
, in patients with type 2 diabetes who are not yet on insulin, nateglinide is a useful alternative to sulfonylureae.
, in the short term, the new insulin secretagogs are no better than the older ones in terms of glycemic control, hypoglycemic risk, or β-cell preservation.
